en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on the Indivisible, from the Section of Puzzling Questions.
2. The Question on the Undeclared Matters “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
‘Ānanda, the Tathāgata has no teacher’s fist regarding the Dhammas. Yet again, when questioned by the Elder Māluṅkyaputta, he did not provide an answer.”
“Venerable Nāgasena, this question has two ends and must depend on one side or the other, either through ignorance or through secrecy.
Venerable Nāgasena, if it was said by the Blessed One:
‘Ānanda, there is no “teacher’s fist” regarding the Dhammas of the Tathāgata,’ then it follows that the Elder Māluṅkyaputta’s question was not answered because of ignorance.”
“If it was not declared because he knew [the answer], then there is a teacher’s closed fist regarding the Dhammas of the Tathāgata.
This too is a double-pronged question that has come to you; it must be resolved by you.
“Great King, this has also been said by the Blessed One: ‘Ānanda, there is no teacher’s closed fist regarding the Dhammas of the Tathāgata.’”
And the question asked by the Elder Māluṅkyaputta was left undeclared by the Thera, not because he did not know it, nor because he intended to conceal it.
"Great King, there are these four ways of answering questions.
Which are the four?"
There is the question to be answered categorically, the question to be answered analytically, the question to be answered with a counter-question, and the question to be set aside.
And what, Great King, is the question to be answered categorically?
"Form is impermanent"—this is a question to be answered categorically.
‘Feeling is impermanent’ …pe… ‘Perception is impermanent’ …pe… ‘Volitional formations are impermanent’ …pe…
‘Consciousness is impermanent’: this is a question to be answered categorically; this is a question to be answered categorically.
What is a question to be answered by way of analysis?
‘But is form impermanent?’—this is a question to be answered by way of analysis.
‘But feeling is impermanent’ …pe… ‘But perception is impermanent’ …pe… ‘But volitional formations are impermanent’ …pe…
‘But is consciousness impermanent?’—this is a question to be answered by way of analysis; this is a question to be answered by way of analysis.
What is a question to be answered by way of cross-questioning?
‘Does one cognize everything with the eye?’—this is a question to be answered by way of cross-questioning.
What is a question to be set aside?
"The world is eternal" is a question to be set aside; "the world is not eternal," [is a question to be set aside].
‘The world is finite,’ ‘the world is infinite,’ ‘the world is both finite and infinite.’
‘The world is neither finite nor infinite,’ ‘the soul and the body are the same,’ ‘the soul is one thing and the body another.’
‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death.’
‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’—this is a question to be set aside;
this is a question to be set aside.
Great King, the Blessed One did not answer that question to be set aside for the elder Māluṅkyaputta.
But for what reason is that question to be set aside?
Because there is no cause or reason for its elucidation; therefore, that question is to be set aside.
There is no utterance of speech by the Blessed Buddhas that is without cause or without reason.”
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! This is so; I accept it as such.
Thus ends the second question on the undeclared points.
